item.title: Slamdance Film Festival 2027: DIG (Digital, Interactive and Gaming)
item.description:
Organisation: Slamdance

Location: Los Angeles, California, United States (festival 18-24 February 2027). Open to international entries.

Award: Festival exhibition at Slamdance in Los Angeles. DIG welcomes interactive documentaries, VR/AR, experiential installations, and genre-bending games. Entry fees: USD 60 regular, USD 70 late, USD 90 extended/final.

Duration: Festival 18-24 February 2027.

Deadline: 06 Oct 2026

Slamdance's DIG (Digital, Interactive and Gaming) showcase presents work at the edges of cinema and interactivity: interactive documentaries, VR/AR, experiential installations, and experimental games, a strong fit for interactive AI and data-driven work. Film categories run on similar deadline tiers. DIG deadlines: regular 10 August 2026 (USD 60), late 14 September 2026 (USD 70), extended 6 October 2026 (USD 90).

item.title: Digital Cultures Festival 2026: Best of Poland Open Call
item.description:
Organisation: Digital Cultures Festival (Monster Mind Studio); Pitch Award funded by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute

Location: Warsaw, Poland (live pitches on 24 September 2026)

Award: Best of Poland Pitch Award: a career development grant of up to PLN 5,000 (funded by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute) for the jury's top pick, to support participation in a European industry event. Up to 10 creators also receive pitch coaching and expert feedback. No application fee.

Duration: Live 7-minute pitch showcase on 24 September 2026

Deadline: Closed 01 Aug 2026

Best of Poland is the Digital Cultures Festival's showcase for work at the intersection of art and technology. Open to anyone working creatively in digital media (artists, filmmakers, game developers, UX designers, programmers, curators, students and more) with projects that show how technology fosters genuine human connection and addresses contemporary social change. Eligible formats include VR, AR, interactive film, games, net art and cross-media works; both completed and in-progress projects qualify. Selected creators present 7-minute live pitches on 24 September 2026 in Warsaw; the jury's top pick receives the Best of Poland Pitch Award, a career development grant of up to PLN 5,000 funded by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute to support participation in a European industry event, and up to 10 creators receive pitch coaching with festival director Anna Szylar and expert feedback. Free to apply via the form on the festival site. Deadline: 1 August 2026.

item.title: ProAC / Fomento CultSP: Edital 05/2026, Electronic Games Development and Publishing
item.description:
Organisation: Secretaria da Cultura, Economia e Industria Criativas do Estado de Sao Paulo (ProAC)

Location: Sao Paulo state, Brazil. Open only to legal entities headquartered in Sao Paulo state for at least two years.

Award: BRL 300,000 (around USD 55,000 / EUR 50,000) per selected project, 20 projects total across two modules, from a BRL 6,000,000 pool. Registration is free.

Duration: Module I funds game development; Module II funds finalisation and publishing of an existing game.

Deadline: Closed 27 Jul 2026

Sao Paulo state's ProAC scheme runs one of the largest dedicated public funds for game development in Latin America. Edital 05/2026 splits BRL 6,000,000 across two modules of ten projects each: Module I for developing electronic games, Module II for finalising and publishing them, at BRL 300,000 per project. At least six of the ten slots in each module are reserved for applicants based outside the state capital. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED AND NARROW: individuals cannot apply. Applicants must be legal entities, meaning private companies (for-profit or not-for-profit) or registered MEI microentrepreneurs, headquartered in Sao Paulo state for at least two years, with artistic or cultural activity expressly stated in their founding documents. Applications close 27 July 2026 at 23:59:59 Brasilia time via fomento.sp.gov.br. Note this is a tight deadline.

Open call details

item.title: UK Global Screen Fund: International Distribution, Video Game Release Funding
item.description:
Organisation: British Film Institute (UK Global Screen Fund, backed by DCMS)

Location: United Kingdom (applications from the UK-based lead development studio)

Award: Non-recoupable grant towards international marketing and release activity; the award range is not published on the fund page. A cap of GBP 625,000 applies across all UKGSF strands per organisation over any three-year period. No application fee.

Duration: Single release-activity award; apply no later than eight weeks before the funded activity begins.

Deadline: 14 Aug 2026

The newest strand of the UK Global Screen Fund extends the fund's international-distribution logic from film into UK independent narrative video games. It supports marketing and release activity for games with demonstrable international appeal and sales potential, awarding non-recoupable grants to help UK studios reach overseas players. ELIGIBILITY: applications must be made by the UK-based development studio deemed the lead developer for the game, and only narrative video games qualify. One application per game. The wider UKGSF requirement that applicants be independent screen-sector companies registered and centrally managed in the UK applies. TIMING: the round opened 14 May 2026 and closes at 12pm on Friday 14 August 2026, making it one of the few hard-deadline BFI opportunities currently live. Separately, applications must be filed at least eight weeks before the funded activity starts, so a game releasing in early autumn may fall outside the window even if the application lands before 14 August. NOTE: award amounts are not published on the fund page, so treat the range as unknown rather than estimated. A cumulative cap of GBP 625,000 per organisation across all UK Global Screen Fund strands over any three-year period also applies.

Open call details

item.title: Game Design Emerging Talents: Production
item.description:
Organisation: Pro Helvetia (Swiss Arts Council)

Location: Switzerland-based emerging game studios.

Award: Up to CHF 50,000, requiring a matching grant of equal value from own or third-party funding. No application fee.

Duration: Production phase; deadlines twice yearly (1 March and 1 September).

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Pro Helvetia's Game Design Emerging Talents production grant funds the production of digital games based on advanced prototypes or vertical slices. Emerging Talents are studios whose game-design education or company foundation dates back less than seven years. Applicants must be legal entities (sole proprietorships accepted if willing to convert). ELIGIBILITY: requires a connection to Switzerland (Swiss citizenship, or permanent residency with regular artistic activity in Switzerland); not open to practitioners without a Swiss connection. At least 50 percent of participants must be Swiss citizens or permanent residents whose place of work is in Switzerland. AMOUNT: up to CHF 50,000, requiring a matching grant of equal value from own or third-party funding. Deadlines twice a year: 1 March (23:59 CET) and 1 September (23:59 CEST). Apply via the Pro Helvetia portal.

Open call details

item.title: Game Design Emerging Talents: She Got Game (Switzerland)
item.description:
Organisation: Pro Helvetia (Swiss Arts Council)

Location: Professional game designers from Switzerland who identify as women.

Award: CHF 3,000 toward prototype/demo production, plus mentoring, community access, and potential trade-fair access; up to CHF 250 per week childcare support for international events. No application fee.

Duration: Six-month mentoring programme (approximately 30 hours total); notification November 2026.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

She Got Game is a Pro Helvetia mentoring programme promoting equal opportunities for women in the Swiss and international game industry, supporting the representation of women in management positions through dialogue with experienced international experts. This is the variant for professional game designers FROM Switzerland who identify as women (a separate variant exists for practitioners in the liaison-office regions). Emerging Talents are developers or studios whose relevant training or registration dates back less than seven years. ELIGIBILITY: requires a connection to Switzerland (Swiss citizenship, or permanent residency with regular artistic activity in Switzerland); not open to practitioners without a Swiss connection. WHAT IS OFFERED: individual coaching on project development, business strategy, finances, marketing, PR, and pitch training; a growing community of female game developers; potential access to international trade fairs; CHF 3,000 toward a prototype or demo; and up to CHF 250 per week toward childcare or children's travel when attending trade fairs. Roughly 30 hours over six months. Submission deadline 1 September 2026 (23:59 CEST); notification November 2026. Apply via the Pro Helvetia portal.

Open call details

item.title: Game Design Emerging Talents: She Got Game
item.description:
Organisation: Pro Helvetia (Swiss Arts Council)

Location: Remote/international mentoring programme; applicants must be based in one of Pro Helvetia's liaison-office regions (Arab region, East Asia, South America, South Asia and Vietnam, and West, Central, East and Southern Africa).

Award: CHF 3,000 toward the production of a prototype or demo version, plus individual coaching and community access; potential access to international trade fairs. When attending trade fairs, applicants with childcare responsibilities can request up to CHF 250 per week for childcare or children's travel expenses. No application fee.

Duration: Six-month mentoring programme, approximately 30 hours total commitment; notification in November 2026; earliest project start 1 January 2027.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

She Got Game is a Pro Helvetia mentoring programme promoting equal opportunities in the Swiss and international game industry, supporting the representation of women in management positions through dialogue with experienced international experts from the game industry. The call is aimed at professional game designers who identify as women from the regions of Pro Helvetia's liaison offices: the Arab region, East Asia, South America, South Asia and Vietnam, and West, Central, East and Southern Africa. ELIGIBILITY: Emerging Talents are game developers or game studios whose relevant training or registration (self-employed, sole proprietorship, or company) dates back less than seven years. Selection criteria include digital content for devices such as computers, consoles, mobile devices, or mixed-reality devices requiring a high level of interaction; clearly defined objectives in terms of participation and career; originality, feasibility, degree of innovation, and marketability of the project; and project leaders holding the copyright and rights of use. Excluded: commissioned work and projects that are part of an advertising or promotional campaign, and purely technological projects without obvious narrative and/or aesthetic content. WHAT IS OFFERED: individual coaching and input talks on project development, business strategy and finances, marketing, PR, and pitch training; involvement in a growing community of female game developers; potential access to international trade fairs; CHF 3,000 toward the production of a prototype or demo version; and up to CHF 250 per week toward childcare or children's travel expenses when attending international trade fairs (a budget must be presented in advance). All modules are conducted in English; the programme is a time-consuming commitment of roughly 30 hours over six months, plus potential additional time attending events or trade fairs. APPLICATION: submit a short CV (including education/training, nationality, and residency status in Switzerland), a short description of the current project (type and genre, gameplay, platform, development status, target audience, with relevant visual material, max. 10 A4 pages), a project portfolio, and expectations regarding the programme's objectives. All documents should be submitted in English; if not possible, applications may be submitted in German, French, or Italian. KEY DATES: applications open 1 July 2026; submission deadline 1 September 2026, 23:59 CEST; notification of decision in November 2026; earliest project start 1 January 2027. Apply via the Pro Helvetia application portal.

item.title: Feminist Gaming Fellowship: Open Call 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Feminist Gaming Project

Location: Remote across the Netherlands, Türkiye, Germany, and the UK

Award: EUR 1,000 honorarium per fellow (paid half at the start, half on completion)

Duration: Three months, August to October 2026; minimum ~6 hours per week (~75 hours total)

Deadline: Closed 12 Jul 2026

The Feminist Gaming Project is opening applications for its first Fellowship cohort: five fellows from different creative and research fields spending three months developing 3D assets, tools, and documentation for its Open Access Asset Library (OAL), a free, open repository of inclusive 3D content created by, with, and for intersectionally feminist and diverse communities. Where mainstream marketplaces default to hyper-athletic, idealized, or hyper-sexualized characters, the OAL offers average bodies, real postures, everyday objects, and the kinds of lives most games leave out (pregnancy and postpartum, care work, ageing, disability, domestic labor). This first cohort is dedicated to 3D content. Supported by the Creative Industries Fund NL and working across the Netherlands, Türkiye, Germany, and the UK, the project challenges exclusionary norms in how games are made. The fellowship offers a EUR 1,000 honorarium per fellow over three months (half at start, half on completion); mentorship from the core team and advisors in feminist design, game studies, 3D production, and digital culture; a peer community across NL, TR, DE, and the UK with biweekly meetings; visibility through a travelling exhibition program, publications, and public events; and authorship credited in the OAL under its license terms. Five roles are recruited (one fellow each): 3D Character Artist for inclusive base meshes; 3D Character Artist for pregnancy and postpartum assets; 3D Animator for neutral and everyday movement; 3D Modeller for domestic and care-labor environments; and Researcher/Writer for documentation and the representation framework; applicants may rank up to two. Open to 3D artists, animators, modellers, designers, researchers, and writers committed to inclusive and intersectional representation in games; prior game-industry experience is not required, and emerging creators, underrepresented practitioners, and researchers at the intersection of games, gender, and culture are especially encouraged, particularly those based in or connected to NL, TR, DE, or the UK. To apply, email feministgamingproject@gmail.com with a short statement (max ~500 words), a portfolio or work samples (a link is fine), and confirmation of availability for the three-month period; name the role(s) in the subject line or statement. The project explicitly asks applicants to write statements in their own voice rather than using AI-generated text. Indicative timeline: applications close 12 July 2026; selection and notification late July; fellowship period August to October 2026; showcase and publication November to December 2026.

item.title: PLAY26 Creative Gaming Festival: Open Call for Games & Playful Media Works
item.description:
Organisation: PLAY - Creative Gaming Festival

Location: Hamburg, Germany; international submissions welcome (with a Focus Hamburg feature for artists and developers based in Hamburg).

Award: Exhibition and awards opportunity, NOT a paid grant: selected works are showcased to an international festival audience. Awards include the Most Creative Game Award and an Audience Award (all games in the festival exhibition are eligible, voted on by festival visitors). No artist fee is stated.

Duration: Festival 2026 (exhibition and awards show)

Deadline: Closed 28 Jun 2026

PLAY is all about the creative use of digital games, combining this culture with media art, discourse and education. This year's theme, 'Hey, listen! (Music & Emotion)', relates to mixtape culture and the sharing of bonds and feelings with the people you like and love. The open call invites artists and developers to submit games or playful media works (including alt.ctrl, interactive theatre and performances) for one of three strands: the Creative Gaming Awards (works that let players get creative in or with them, including the Most Creative Game Award); the core exhibition 'Hey, listen!' (works fitting this year's Music & Emotion theme); and Focus Hamburg (a Local Artists Feature for artists and developers based in Hamburg). All games shown in the festival exhibition are eligible for the Audience Award, chosen by festival visitors and honoured at the Awards Show. Selected projects are showcased to an international audience. NOTE: this is a festival exhibition and awards open call rather than a paid grant; no artist fee is stated. The Call for Games & Playful Media Works is open until 28 June 2026 (Calls for Talks and Workshops follow). Submit via https://www.playfestival.de/en/play26-submissions-are-open.

item.title: VH AWARD 2026 (Hyundai Motor Group)
item.description:
Organisation: Hyundai Motor Group

Location: Online residency (global exhibitions); for artists engaging with Asia

Award: Each of five finalists receives a USD 30,000 production grant plus an Ars Electronica online residency; the Grand Prix winner receives an additional USD 30,000 (USD 60,000 total). Honorary Mentions join selected residency components. No application fee.

Duration: Online residency Sep 2026 - Mar 2027 (finalists); award ceremony and exhibitions June 2027

Deadline: Closed 21 Jul 2026

The VH AWARD, hosted by Hyundai Motor Group, supports emerging media artists whose work engages with the context of Asia, through an online residency and exhibitions across global platforms. FIELD: audiovisual, screen-based artworks including video art, motion graphics, animation, games, films or newly explored areas; proposals must suit single-channel video presentation (no interactivity). ELIGIBILITY: individuals or collectives whose work engages with the context of Asia, including artists of Asian descent, those based in Asia, and the Asian diaspora. Five finalists are selected, each receiving a USD 30,000 production grant and a place in the Ars Electronica online residency program (masterclasses and 1:1 mentoring), with networking and exhibition opportunities; one Grand Prix recipient (announced 2027) receives an additional USD 30,000; a new Honorary Mention category recognises one or two further applicants with website features and selected residency components. APPLY: via the VH AWARD website Entry Portal with a video portfolio (max 3 min), CV and artist statement (max 3 pages), and a new artwork proposal (max 3 pages) with a reference video (max 1 min); all documents in English; proposed works must be original and unexhibited. Open call 26 May - 21 July 2026 (KST); finalists announced September 2026.
